title: Deeper/broader cross-peer validation protocol and DXF loss-boundary audit
mode: primary-source web research and plan-only update
scope: Inspect peer regression harnesses for machine-verifiable semantic assertions versus interactive diff workflows
Separate strict DXF parsing from recovery/audit and cross-document import/projection
Refine implementation-ready peer evidence capture without increasing per-slice validation time

method.kind: Read current primary repository scripts and project documentation
method.limitations: Mutable upstream master/stable pages were reviewed as route-contract evidence only. No peer behavior was executed or independently reproduced. The ODA v5.4.1 specification remains authoritative for DWG byte layout.

sources.observed: test-dxf.sh builds and converts a selected drawing, filters output, and sends a diff through a comparator and interactive pager; it is a useful inspection aid, not by itself a machine-verifiable semantic regression result. Project documentation separately describes direction/version coverage limits.

Recovery repairs structurally flawed ASCII DXF and audits the result; documents can be returned with unrecoverable binary-XRECORD decode errors. The docs warn recovered rewrites can lose information or become invalid and describe strict decoding as an alternative.

The deprecated compatibility importer is a cross-document graphical transfer route. It explicitly removes extension dictionaries, AppData, and XDATA, omits OBJECTS and selected overrides, and requires finalization for dependencies. These limitations do not describe the base parser.

The reader example shows OnNotification warnings/information during Read(), and the README lists format-direction/version capability. These are useful diagnostics and route hints but do not constitute a complete per-object semantic-loss ledger.
